title: Using straps will help you grow your forearms
summary: NH argues non-competing lifters should use straps on pulls so the back and legs, not grip, limit the lift, and that straps actually help forearm growth by saving grip and CNS freshness for direct wrist and elbow flexion work. He dismisses hook grip as a 'biological strap' and mixed grip, and says his forearms stagnated during two years of strapless pulling but blew up with direct isolation.

claims.claim: With a double-overhand grip, grip limits floor pulls 100% of the time; no lifter has forearms stronger than their posterior chain.
The deadlift is a posterior-chain exercise, not a grip or forearm exercise; straps let you focus it on back and legs.
Critics contradict themselves calling straps both useless and cheating; if they let you pull more they're not useless, and pulling with good form isn't ego.
Unless you're a powerlifter, use straps on pulls; there's no reason for hook grip, and mixed grip is especially terrible.
NH pulls more with a mixed grip than with straps/double overhand; straps don't necessarily let everyone lift more.
Heavy double-overhand or mixed-grip deadlifts won't grow forearms much; crushing grip isn't what grows them.
Elite natural sumo pullers moving 600 lbs with a mixed grip often have stick forearms: grip strength doesn't correlate with forearm size.
Forearm hypertrophy comes from wrist flexion and elbow flexion; pulls and static holds grow only certain parts to an extent.
Forearm activation is the same whether you pull from the floor or above the knee, so heavy high rack pulls held 5 seconds (e.g. 700 lbs) beat 500 from the floor for forearm growth.
If you dislike straps, do most working sets with your regular grip and use straps for volume work.
Hook grip is a 'biological strap'; the only difference from straps is ego, plus it's uncomfortable, slow to learn and impossible for some hands.
NH's palm is wider and longer than his fingers, making hook grip physically impossible for him.
He uses double overhand where it doesn't hurt performance and straps for everything else; straps build the back faster because the back is far stronger than the forearms.
Never rely on pulls to grow forearms; direct forearm work needs wrist and elbow flexions that move the muscle through a range of motion in different positions.
Mixed grip works by one hand counter-rotating the bar; straps do the same while avoiding biceps tears.
NH has scoliosis, so his back sits naturally to one side; he pulled all his deadlifts mixed grip when he cared about numbers and loved it.
Heavy static gripping fatigues the whole forearm and CNS without yielding hypertrophy, leaving grip too tired for next-day forearm work.
NH does reverse EZ-bar curls for 10 sets of 10 (100 reps), which needs a fresh grip.
Pulling raw without straps for two years grew his deadlift and back while his forearms stagnated; once he did direct flexion and isolation work they blew up.
Use straps wherever grip limits the lift or stops you working the upper back, then spend the saved grip on forearm exercises.
